title: Hooks & Auto-save
lead: Background filing that keeps memory off the chat window and under budget.
summary: The hooks system (Stop and PreCompact) auto-saves session transcripts to the palace in the background without blocking the chat window. The Stop hook fires every 15 human messages (configurable) to checkpoint the conversation; the PreCompact hook saves everything just before context compression. Both hooks mine the JSONL transcript directly into drawers, then optionally ingest project files and notify the AI via systemMessage (silent mode, default v3.3.0+) or block the AI to save via MCP tools (legacy). This design saves approximately USD 1 per session by eliminating token retransmission of diary blocks in the chat.

concepts.definition: Claude Code event fired after each assistant response; counts human messages in the transcript and triggers auto-save when a threshold (SAVE_INTERVAL=15) is reached.
Claude Code event fired right before context compression; always runs a synchronous mine to capture transcript data before the AI loses detailed context.
Default (v3.3.0+) hook behavior: saves directly via Python API without returning decision:block; the AI sees only a systemMessage notification, zero chat window interruption.
Hook-spawned mines run as fully detached processes using POSIX start_new_session or Windows process groups, so the hook exits immediately and the background work continues.

Atomic slot-based deduplication in ~/.mempalace/hook_state/mine_pids/: prevents concurrent mines of the same target by using O_CREAT|O_EXCL and per-target hash digests; stale PIDs are detected by age.
If ~/.mempalace/ is removed or is not a directory, all hook side effects (mining, logging, state creation) short-circuit immediately without disk access.
Boolean setting (default True, hooks.auto_save) that gates all Stop and PreCompact hook functionality; when False, hooks pass through silently.
Hooks infer the project wing name from the JSONL transcript using: (1) cwd metadata, (2) encoded .claude/projects/ path decoding, (3) legacy -Projects- segment, or (4) default wing_sessions.

symbols.name: hook_stop
symbols.role: Main Stop hook handler; counts messages, checks threshold, spawns mines or saves directly, handles silent vs. blocking modes.

symbols.name: hook_precompact
symbols.role: PreCompact hook handler; runs synchronous mine before context compression, always saves without threshold gate.

symbols.name: _spawn_mine
symbols.role: Spawns a detached background subprocess for mining after atomically claiming a per-target PID slot.

symbols.name: _mine_already_running
symbols.role: Checks if a previous mine for the same target is still alive (via PID liveness or age) to prevent concurrent miners of the same source.

symbols.name: _claim_mine_slot
symbols.role: Atomically reserves a per-target PID file using O_CREAT|O_EXCL, with stale-reclaim logic.

symbols.name: _save_diary_direct
symbols.role: Silent-mode save: calls mcp_server.tool_diary_write directly to write a checkpoint entry without MCP roundtrip.

symbols.name: _wing_from_transcript_path
symbols.role: Derives project wing name from transcript path: cwd metadata → path decoding → fallback to wing_sessions.

symbols.name: _detached_popen_kwargs
symbols.role: Returns subprocess.Popen kwargs for fully detached child processes (POSIX start_new_session, Windows creationflags).

symbols.name: _palace_root_exists
symbols.role: User-removable kill-switch: returns False if ~/.mempalace is missing or not a directory, short-circuiting all hook side effects.

symbols.name: SAVE_INTERVAL
symbols.role: Human message threshold for triggering Stop hook save (default 15, configurable).

symbols.name: MempalaceConfig.hooks_auto_save
symbols.role: Boolean config (default True) that gates all Stop and PreCompact hook functionality; False disables hooks.

symbols.name: MempalaceConfig.hook_silent_save
symbols.role: Boolean config (default True) that switches between silent-mode (Python API) and legacy blocking-mode (MCP tools).

surprises.title: Stop Hook Runs Asynchronously (Background Mining), PreCompact Runs Synchronously
surprises.detail: Stop hook spawns mines with _spawn_mine (background via detached subprocess & flag in shell), exiting immediately to stay under 500ms budget. PreCompact hook uses subprocess.run (synchronous), blocking until the mine completes. This split design: Stop optimizes latency (background work), PreCompact optimizes safety (sync ensures data is saved before compaction loses it).

surprises.title: Windows Process Detection Cannot Use os.kill(pid, 0)
surprises.detail: On Windows, os.kill(sig) terminates the process (maps to TerminateProcess). The code uses ctypes to call GetExitCodeProcess instead. If the call fails or process handle is invalid, it returns False (dead). This cross-platform difference is buried in a utility function but is critical for correctness.

surprises.title: Silent Mode Defaults to True on Config Read Failure
surprises.detail: When hook_silent_save config is unreadable (missing, corrupted, or AttributeError), the code defaults to True (silent mode) rather than blocking. Safe-default design: if config breaks, save in background so users don't lose data or get stuck in an infinite block loop. The fallback is logged as a WARNING.

surprises.title: Token Savings of USD ~1/session via Background Mining
surprises.detail: Previous versions asked the AI to write diary entries in chat, costing ~USD 1 per session in token retransmission. v3.3.0+ silent mode saves directly via Python API (tool_diary_write), so the AI never writes diary blocks in chat. The systemMessage notification (✦ N memories...) is negligible. This alone justifies the shift from blocking to silent mode.

surprises.title: Hook Timeout is 30s But Mine Timeout is 60s+
surprises.detail: The hook command timeout in .claude/settings.local.json is 30 seconds (harness kills the hook if it takes longer). But the mine subprocess itself can run up to 60+ seconds (timeout=60 in precompact subprocess.run, or unlimited if MEMPALACE_MINE_TIMEOUT_HOURS > 0.05 hours). The hook spawns the mine and exits; the mine runs independently in background. This architecture keeps hook latency under 500ms (performance budget) while allowing substantive work.

surprises.title: Shell Hook Uses sed Instead of bash 4+ mapfile
surprises.detail: macOS ships bash 3.2.57 (Apple's GPLv3 cutoff, 2006), which lacks mapfile/readarray (bash 4.0+). The shell hook parses Python output via sed -n 'Np' (classic, portable) instead of mapfile. Without this, every value would fall back to default on macOS and hooks would silently produce zero saves (issue #1440). This is a subtle portability gotcha.

surprises.title: Wing Derivation Tries cwd Metadata First (Most Reliable)
surprises.detail: The wing name derivation (_wing_from_transcript_path) checks the JSONL transcript for embedded cwd metadata first, before decoding the transcript path. This is the most reliable method because Claude Code records the working directory on most message types. Only if cwd is missing does it fall back to path decoding (heuristic) or defaults to wing_sessions. This priority order avoids silent misclassification.

designDecisions.decision: Background Subprocess (Detached) vs. Inline Synchronous Mining
designDecisions.rationale: Hooks must return to Claude Code within 500ms (performance budget). Spawning a detached subprocess allows the hook to exit immediately while mining continues in the background. PreCompact is an exception: it mines synchronously because compaction must wait for the transcript to be saved. This split design respects both latency and data safety.

designDecisions.decision: Silent Mode (Python API) as Default, Blocking Mode (MCP) as Legacy
designDecisions.rationale: MISSION.md goal: remove noise from chat window and eliminate token retransmission of diary blocks. Silent mode (v3.3.0+) saves via direct Python API call, costing zero tokens and keeping the chat clean. Blocking mode asks the AI to save via MCP tools but costs tokens and interrupts flow. Silent mode is the default; blocking mode is opt-in for backward compatibility.

designDecisions.decision: Per-target PID Slots Instead of Global mine.pid File
designDecisions.rationale: Different mine targets (different dirs, modes, wings) must run in parallel. A single global PID file either blocks unrelated targets or allows concurrent miners of the same target (corrupting the HNSW index). Per-target slots allow concurrent miners of different targets while deduplicating miners of the same target. Atomic O_CREAT|O_EXCL prevents race conditions between simultaneous hook fires.

Users need a clean way to disable MemPalace without uninstalling hooks. Removing ~/.mempalace is the user-visible kill-switch. It prevents hooks from touching disk, creating state dirs, or logging, allowing complete opt-out. The check happens before any side effect (logging, mining) so even the absence signal itself is not logged, respecting user intent.

designDecisions.decision: Wing Name Derivation: cwd Metadata → Path Decoding → Fallback
designDecisions.rationale: Project wing names must be inferred from the transcript path since they are not explicitly provided by the harness. cwd metadata (from JSONL) is the most reliable source. Path decoding is a heuristic fallback for transcripts not under .claude/projects. Default to wing_sessions if both fail. This hierarchy prioritizes correctness and avoids silent misclassification.

related.why: Hooks are a critical component of the overall MemPalace pipeline, fitting into the data flow from harness to palace storage.
PreCompact and Stop hooks invoke the conversation miner to ingest transcripts before compaction or on schedule.
Silent mode calls mcp_server.tool_diary_write directly; hooks are integrated with the tool layer via direct Python function calls.
Hooks are invoked via CLI dispatcher (cmd_hook) and implement the hook event handlers (session-start, stop, precompact).
Hook logs and PID slots live in ~/.mempalace/hook_state/; stale slot cleanup and debuggging are maintenance tasks.
Hooks respect the palace root kill-switch and never access external APIs; all work is local, protecting user data.

searchDoc.title: Hooks & Auto-save
searchDoc.summary: Two Claude Code hooks (Stop and PreCompact) auto-save session transcripts to the palace in the background without blocking the chat window, saving roughly USD 1 per session by writing diary entries via a direct Python API call instead of retyping them in chat.
searchDoc.body: MemPalace ships two Claude Code hooks, Stop and PreCompact, that auto-save session transcripts into the palace without interrupting the chat window. The Stop hook fires after each assistant response, counts human (non-command-message) entries in the session JSONL transcript, and triggers a checkpoint when the count since the last save reaches SAVE_INTERVAL (default 15, configurable). When the threshold is met it logs state, derives the project wing name from the transcript path, and spawns detached background mining subprocesses for the transcript in convos mode and an optional MEMPAL_DIR in projects mode. The PreCompact hook fires just before context compression; unlike Stop it does not count messages or gate on a threshold, instead running a synchronous blocking mine so the transcript is physically filed before the AI loses access to it, then returning empty JSON so compaction proceeds. The Stop hook optimizes latency (background work, under a 500ms budget) while PreCompact optimizes safety (synchronous save). Silent mode, the default since v3.3.0, saves the diary entry directly by calling tool_diary_write from the MCP server as a Python function, then returns only a systemMessage notification, eliminating token retransmission of diary blocks and saving about USD 1 per session. Legacy blocking mode instead returns decision block to ask the AI to save manually via MCP tools mempalace_diary_write and mempalace_add_drawer; the stop_hook_active flag prevents infinite loops. Hook-spawned miners claim atomic per-target PID slots in ~/.mempalace/hook_state/mine_pids using os.open with O_CREAT O_EXCL, hashing the mine command of directory, mode, and wing into a slot filename to prevent concurrent mines of the same source while allowing distinct targets to run in parallel; stale slots are reclaimed by PID liveness or age, default 2 hours via MEMPALACE_MINE_TIMEOUT_HOURS. Detached subprocesses use POSIX start_new_session or Windows DETACHED_PROCESS, CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, and CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB flags so the hook can exit immediately. The palace-root kill-switch _palace_root_exists checks that ~/.mempalace is a directory; if the user removes it, all hooks short-circuit before any disk access. The hooks.auto_save config (default True) gates all hook functionality. Wing derivation reads cwd metadata first, then path decoding, then defaults to wing_sessions. On Windows, liveness uses ctypes GetExitCodeProcess rather than os.kill which would terminate the process. macOS bash 3.2 lacks mapfile, so the shell hook parses Python output with sed. A safe default selects silent mode when the config is unreadable. The hook harness timeout is 30 seconds while the mine subprocess can run 60 or more seconds independently in the background.
